slot.brief: Doppler effect: a source and observer moving relative to each other (both approach, or one recedes); compute the apparent frequency heard, or ratio of approach to recede frequencies.

stem: A stationary observer hears a source of frequency $500$ Hz as it moves first towards and then away from the observer at $34$ m s$^{-1}$. If the speed of sound is $340$ m s$^{-1}$, the ratio of the two heard frequencies (approaching to receding) is

verdicts.working: For a moving source, the approaching and receding frequencies are proportional to \(v/(v-v_s)\) and \(v/(v+v_s)\). Their ratio is \((340+34)/(340-34)=11/9\).

working:
$\dfrac{f_{\rm app}}{f_{\rm rec}}=\dfrac{v+v_s}{v-v_s}=\dfrac{340+34}{340-34}$\\
$=\dfrac{374}{306}=\dfrac{11}{9}$

Independent check: For a moving source, the approaching and receding frequencies are proportional to \(v/(v-v_s)\) and \(v/(v+v_s)\). Their ratio is \((340+34)/(340-34)=11/9\).
solution:
For a moving source, $f_{\rm app}=f\dfrac{v}{v-v_s}$ and $f_{\rm rec}=f\dfrac{v}{v+v_s}$. Hence,
$$\frac{f_{\rm app}}{f_{\rm rec}}=\frac{v+v_s}{v-v_s}=\frac{340+34}{340-34}=\frac{11}{9}.$$
